items.label: Consumer sentiment (University of Michigan)
items.value_label: 48.0, October final (Oct 23), revised up from the 46.3 preliminary
items.say: Still among the lowest readings in the survey's history; the final October figure was revised up to nearly September's level.

items.label: Gasoline, national average (AAA)
items.compare: $3.038 a year ago; $4.270 a week ago; $4.456 a month ago
items.say: Up about 39% in a year, though 4 cents lower than a week ago and 23 cents below a month ago.

items.label: A Chipotle chicken burrito bowl
items.say: Roughly 15–20% more than four years ago; restaurant prices overall are up 3.4% in the past year (CPI food away from home, August).
items.src: Reuters via ThePricer (May 2026); Food Business News (Oct 2022)

items.label: Prediction markets: Democratic House
items.compare: Senate: about 69% Democratic from the balance-of-power contracts (Democrats win both 67.5¢ on Kalshi and 70.5¢ on Polymarket; Democratic House with Republican Senate 25.5¢ and 23.5¢; Republican House with Democratic Senate under 1¢; Republicans win both 7.1¢ and 6.5¢); DeFi Rate's Senate page puts the Democrats' chance at 69% on Oct 30, with Kansas (51% Democratic) and Iowa (47%) the closest contracts
items.say: Markets moved toward Democrats in the final week: the House price is up two points and the Senate about four since Oct 28, with Kansas now priced about even.

items.label: Cook Political Report House ratings
items.value_label: 18 toss-ups after 12 more moves toward Democrats (Oct 30)
items.compare: Cook's projection (Oct 30): Democrats flip 12-25 seats, up to 240; Oct 23's table (Solid/Likely/Lean D 220, Toss Up 17, Lean/Likely/Solid R 198) moved Oct 30 by PA-08 and OH-09 to Lean D, CO-05, PA-01 and SC-01 to Toss Up, FL-07, FL-09 and IN-05 to Lean R, and NC-05, NC-09, NJ-02 and WA-05 to Likely R. Senate (Oct 30): Nebraska to Lean R and Florida to Likely R; 7 Toss Ups (Oct 20), 6 Republican-held. Sabato's Crystal Ball (Oct 27): House 225 at least Lean D, 17 Toss-ups, 193 R; Senate 49-46 with 5 Toss-ups
items.say: Democrats need none of the toss-ups for a majority if the seats leaning their way hold; Cook's top of range is now 240.
items.src: Cook Political Report, Oct 30 (House and Senate moves), Oct 20 (Senate Toss Ups); Newsweek, Oct 30; Sabato's Crystal Ball, Oct 27

items.label: House members not seeking re-election
items.value_label: 36 Republicans, 24 Democrats (plus two Democratic delegates); 29 are running for other office
items.say: More Republicans leaving, including 20 running for other office; retirements have not tracked the swing in past midterms.
